lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: Look here, Menippus can judge this. Tell me, Menippus — don’t I look the better-looking of the two?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Who are you two? I ought to know that first, I suppose.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: So which one’s Nireus and which one’s Thersites? Not obvious yet.

lines.speaker: Thersites
lines.text: At least I’ve got this much: I’m no different from you. That blind Homer of yours praised you as the handsomest of all, but even I — bald, scrawny — didn’t come out worse in the judge’s eyes. Go on, Menippus. Tell us which one you think is better-looking.

lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: Me, obviously. Son of Aglaia and Charops. I was the best-looking man who sailed to Troy.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Not down here, though. The bones are all the same. The only difference between your skull and his is that yours is more fragile — delicate, not very manly.

lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: Ask Homer what I looked like when I was fighting with the Achaeans.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Dreams. I can only see what you’ve got now. The old days know what you used to look like.

lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: So I’m not the better-looking one down here, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Neither of you is. In Hades it’s all equal. Everyone looks the same.
